notes: RUNME.BAT is `explo.exe / midi3drv.exe / miglia.exe`; EXPLO.EXE is not part of the game -- emulator.log identifies it as 'Explosive intro by Hard Core. Coded sometime in early 1992', a cracktro that stops on its own text-mode sound-card prompt ([1] Soundblaster [2] Covox [3] Speaker). Earlier probes on this game bypassed it by entering MIDI3DRV.EXE and MIGLIA.EXE directly (skipping the cracktro and its extra prompt entirely); this recipe keeps that bypass. The pre-race key sequence (inherited from the working probe26protection recipe) clicks through the menus/driver-select screens, then answers a copy-protection code-wheel prompt with four 'aaaa' entries at ~206-214 guest seconds. Gameplay (car on the road, dashboard live, RACE TIME ticking) starts by ~213-218 guest seconds. Because that lead-in already consumes past the halfway point of any reasonably-short run, EVERY key in this schedule lands before the race starts (or, for the final five, in its early stretch) -- this deliberately breaks the usual 'all keys in the first half' rule from AGENT-BRIEF.md; that only works here because the game needs no further input to keep driving once the accelerator is held. At 14400000000 cycles (~218 guest-s, right as the race begins) the schedule presses {+up} and never releases it -- {+up}/{-up} is the press only/release only spelling (no bare ASCII equivalent for the arrow key), confirmed against crates/izarravm/src/main.rs text_to_scancode_groups, and 'up' is the accelerate input per Manual.txt ('Joystick up: accelerates'; this DOS build also accepts the keyboard arrow in the same role). Verified in probe27accel (single held key): the speedometer needle visibly advances off zero and the background scenery (houses, an NPC car) changes across screens 0108->0112 while RACE TIME/LEG TIME count down, i.e. real forward motion, not a static frame. Holding the key alone was not enough for a long window: at screen 0112 the game threw a random 'Trouble Screen' breakdown event ('the wheel's jammed... time lost for repairs') that blocks on a mouse-only 'Continue' button, freezing the frame hash for the rest of that probe. probe28dismiss added five \r taps at roughly 1500-2000-cycle*1e6 intervals after the hold (15500000000/17000000000/19000000000/21000000000/23000000000 cycles) purely to dismiss any such dialog that appears while driving; Enter is not a bound driving key per the manual (L/P/space/esc are the only in-race keys documented) so it is a safe no-op during normal driving. With those taps in place the frame hash keeps changing continuously from ~257 to 350 guest seconds (the full tail of the window), i.e. more than 120 guest seconds of sustained on-road motion, confirmed visually: the speedometer needle sits off zero and the road/scenery keep advancing (screens 0134, 0144, 0150 of probe28dismiss; end-frame.ppm of the deep run also shows live gameplay, not a stall). The deep profile window covers roughly guest 0-213s of menu/copy-protection lead-in, then ~213-350s of live driving on the road (car, HUD, RACE/LEG TIME, an NPC car ahead), interrupted at least three more times by 'Trouble Screen' breakdowns that the periodic Enter taps clear. FINDING: real_time_factor was 0.60 on the deep run (486 target is 5.0), well below target, so -BarrierCensus was run; top-3 census rows by unbound_exits were op=0xcf (IRET, unbound=8,250,532, non_continuable), op=0xe3 (JCXZ, unbound=78,781, hard_boundary), and op=0x8e reg=0 memory word (MOV Sreg,r/m, unbound=65,739, call_out_demoted) -- the 0xcf row dominates the total (8.60M unbound exits overall). Also FINDING: pit_writes were 448,720,210 over 350 guest seconds (~1,282,058/guest-s), far above the ~300,000/guest-s latch-poll-storm threshold.
